# Rollback Netcode & Edgegap: Research Notes

Notes from testing an Edgegap UDP relay (`test-relay` v4, match `poc-match-1`) on 2026-11-22, plus reading on
what ping is good for a platform fighter, which games use Edgegap, and how to implement rollback. General
networking knowledge, not Smash-specific; this is not part of `docs/`.

Most Edgegap links are Edgegap's own marketing: treat their numbers as self-reported. Links marked
*(from memory)* were not checked in a search.

## Testing the relay

### What we learned

- **Test the server, not the Users.** The Edgegap "Users" list (eg `83.147.212.59`, `172.58.9.231`) are the
  *players'* IPs, used to pick a location. The server is the **Host IP** (or Host FQDN).
- **Use the external port.** "Ports Mapping" shows external `32454` → internal `7777`: players send to the
  external port; `7777` only exists inside the container. The IP and port change every deployment.
- **UDP has no built-in replies.** Silence from `nc -u` proves nothing; only the server's `pong` (a reply the
  relay code chooses to send) proves the packet arrived.
- **The words matter.** The relay parses the text: `ping N` → `pong N`; `ack N` closes the timer for `ping N`;
  other text (eg `claude-233022-1`) got no reply.
- **"Client N connected" per sender address.** Each `nc` run picks a random source port, so the server sees a
  new client every run. `-p 50000` pins the source port so the `ping` and `ack` come from the same client.
- **Ack = acknowledgement**: "I got your message". TCP acks automatically; UDP doesn't, so games add their own.

### Commands

```bash
# Send one ping (expect "pong 1")
echo -n "ping 1" | nc -u -p 50000 -w1 <host-ip> <external-port>

# Ack it (server logs an RTT, but run by hand it includes your typing time)
echo -n "ack 1" | nc -u -p 50000 -w1 <host-ip> <external-port>

# Real RTT: ack sent the instant the pong arrives
uv run python -c "
import socket, time
s = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM); s.bind(('', 50000)); s.settimeout(2)
srv = ('<host-ip>', <external-port>)
t = time.perf_counter(); s.sendto(b'ping 2', srv)
print(s.recvfrom(1024)[0].decode(), f'{(time.perf_counter() - t) * 1000:.0f} ms (my side)')
s.sendto(b'ack 2', srv)
"

# Interactive session (type lines, see replies; Ctrl+C to quit)
nc -u <host-ip> <external-port>

# Watch packets go out and come back (needs: sudo pacman -S tcpdump)
sudo tcpdump -ni any udp port <external-port>
```

| Part | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `echo -n` | Print the message without a trailing newline (the packet is exactly the text) |
| `\|` | Pipe echo's output into nc |
| `nc -u` | Netcat over UDP (default is TCP) |
| `-p 50000` | Send from source port 50000 (same "client" each run) |
| `-w1` | Wait 1 second for a reply, then exit |

Gotchas: "Address already in use" → port 50000 still held, wait a few seconds. A typo'd port (eg `3007` for
`30073`) fails silently.

### Results (2026-11-22, deployment `64b0d6612e1d`, London)

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| `ping 1`–`3` to `172.239.115.80:32454` (IP and FQDN) | `pong 1`–`3` |
| Python RTT script to `172.239.115.80:30073` | `pong 2 104 ms (my side)` |
| Pings to the Users IPs on `7777` | No reply (wrong target) |

104 ms RTT ≈ 52 ms one way ≈ 3 frames.

## What ping is good for a fighting game

1 frame at 60 fps ≈ 16.7 ms. One player's input travels about half the RTT. Match latency through a relay ≈
half your RTT + half your opponent's.

| RTT | ≈ Frames one way | Feel (with rollback) |
|---|---|---|
| < 50 ms | 0–1 | Offline-like |
| 50–100 ms | 2–3 | Good |
| 100–150 ms | 3–4 | Playable, some visible rollback |
| 150–200 ms | 5–6 | Rough |
| > 200 ms | 6+ | Bad for competitive |

| Source | Says |
|---|---|
| [Infil: netcode p3](https://words.infil.net/w02-netcode-p3.html), [p6](https://words.infil.net/w02-netcode-p6.html) | Delay-based at 100+ ms is unplayable; rollback handles ~150 ms with a couple of rollback frames |
| [Edgegap: Rivals 2 case study](https://edgegap.com/case-studies/aether-studios-rivals-of-aether-2-ii) | Ideal < 20 ms ("extremely challenging"); ping shown in the main UI |
| [Steam: Rivals 2 ping thread](https://steamcommunity.com/app/2217000/discussions/0/601890191585726756) | "Green" up to ~60–66 ms (2 frames delay + 2 rollback ≈ 66 ms); anecdotal |
| [Rivals 2 feedback board](https://rivals-of-aether-ii-patch-160.nolt.io/699) | Players avoid servers at 80+ ms |
| [Riot: how 2XKO handles online play](https://2xko.riotgames.com/en-us/news/dev/how-2xko-handles-online-play/) | Fixed 3 frames input delay, rollback covers the rest |
| [Edgegap: MKX & Injustice 2](https://edgegap.com/blog/game-backend-deep-dive-mortal-kombat-x-injustice-2-rollback) | Rollback works up to 333 ms RTT before pausing |
| [PlayStation: why rollback is better](https://compete.playstation.com/en-us/article/why-is-rollback-netcode-better-for-fighting-games) | General explainer |
| [SmashWiki: Lag Guide](https://ssbwiki.com/User:P.i./Lag_Guide) | Latency ranges from ~0 (CRT offline) to 200 ms (across the world) |

Takeaways: aim for < ~60 ms to the server; < 100 ms fine for casual. **Jitter (spikes) matters more than the
average**: measure 20+ pings and look at the spread. Delay-based netcode (eg Smash Ultimate) feels much worse at
the same ping than rollback.

### How it fits the relay

GGPO-style rollback is peer-to-peer: each player runs the full game and only **inputs** are sent, one small UDP
packet per frame. The relay just forwards input packets between the two players (close to what ping/pong does
now). Rivals 2 goes further with an authoritative server (Snapnet), which is more work.
